digest.component_or_area: MCP server blue-green deployment and session management
propositions: MCP HTTP sessions are stateful and container-sticky; nginx upstream swap to a new container orphans all existing client sessions with opaque 404 Session expired errors instead of reconnect signals
Every 2-minute autodeploy tick that touches MCP_PATHS kills all live agent sessions mid-task because the graceful retire window does not preserve routing, only container lifetime

The default FastMCP configuration uses stateless_http=False, creating per-container session state that cannot survive blue-green cutover; switching to stateless_http=True eliminates the orphaning by making sessions independent of container identity
New clients attempting to connect during the ~22-minute overlap window of two running MCP containers fail with timeout; old container takes time to exit despite upstream already switched
Retired containers accumulate unhealthy and the retire is re-issued on multiple autodeploy ticks before actually terminating, creating a prolonged two-container state

Stateless HTTP mode survives cutovers because requests are independent with no session affinity; verified live across three cutovers with single client session making successful calls on both sides of upstream swaps
